references.title: BLUE HOUR press kit (J.D. Shields, AFI Directing Workshop for Women, 2024; 13 pp, 612x792)
references.what_it_does_well: The closest true peer found (an AFI program short, 2024, 16 min, festival-bound). One typeface, one hue, one running header ('blue hour', tracked, top right of every inside page) and a page number bottom right, so every page is recognisably the same object. Bio pages (p07, p09) hold ONE headshot per page at a fixed size and put every bio in a single measure of ~48 characters; the KEY CREW page (p09) stacks four people with a rotated DIM department label in the gutter, which is the cleanest role|name|bio structure in the whole corpus. The credits page (p11) is a two-column key/value list, roles left, names right, same size, no bold, grouped by blank lines only.
references.take_for_kom: Page 7 (cast). Drop the full-width hero-still-then-paragraphs stack and adopt Blue Hour p09's spine: one column of bios at a fixed measure with the role as a DIM label in the gutter. Concretely: keep ground() with still 40 ghosted as on page 3 (alpha 0.22, scrim 0.50, focus left third), then for each billed actor a row of (a) tracked(c, M, y, ROLE, 'Bask', Z.role, Z.track_r, DIM) at x=74, (b) tracked(c, M+240, y, NAME, 'Bask-SB', SUB, 2.4, CREAM), (c) para(c, bio, M+240, y-34, 640, BODY-0.6, BODY_LEAD-1.5) with fit() guarding height. Four bios of ~110 words each fit at 640 pt measure in roughly 4 x 230 pt = 920 pt, leaving ~700 pt for the BILLED CAST two-column list below, which currently falls off the page. The '7.1' field's provenance block ('DRAFTS, NOT YET APPROVED ...') must be split out of the bio string in epk.json or stripped before para(): that text is a production note, never body copy.
references.avoid: Blue Hour's contrast and scale: 9-10 pt sans on white with the running header in pale blue is legible on a laptop and dead in a projector or on a phone. It also lets one bio run ten lines while the next runs four, so the page reads as unequal weight; KOM should cap each bio with fit() to the same box. And its cover (p01) prints TECHNICAL DETAILS as a caption block on the poster, which KOM's Clean Bank rule already forbids.

references.title: SUPERHERO digital press kit (Émile V. Schlesser, 2020; 18 pp, A4; not a school film but the best-designed short kit in the corpus)
references.what_it_does_well: Every page has one image and one job. The CAST / CREW page (p05) is a set photograph on top and two right-aligned-key / left-aligned-value tables below, names bold, roles light, split on a shared centre axis: exactly the DIM-key / CREAM-value grammar KOM's page 3 already uses, proving the axis-split list works for a crew of 15 without a second column. The bio pages (p07, p09) put the tiny DIM role label ('writer-director', 'cinematographer') ABOVE the big name, not beside it, then a bio at a narrow measure beside a small portrait, then a full-width photograph across the bottom third. The rhythm of every bio page is identical, so the reader stops reading the layout and reads the people.
references.take_for_kom: One structural measurement: the axis-split list. On page 7 and on the credits page 9, put the roles right-aligned to a shared axis and the names left-aligned from that axis plus one gutter, instead of KOM's current left-flush role then a fixed +210 pt name offset (page_cast, col_x + 210) which leaves 'SPECTATOR' and 'KOJO'S MASTER' with unequal gaps. Implement as tracked(c, axis, y, role, 'Bask', BODY, Z.track_r, DIM, 'right') and tracked(c, axis + 24, y, name, 'Bask', 17, Z.track_n, CREAM, 'left'); axis at W/2 = 648 for a single column, 28 pt leading as now. This is the same move page 3 makes with its right margin at 1222 and is why page 3 feels resolved.
references.avoid: Its poster-frame device (a torn-paper drop shadow under every image, p03) and the bold-on-every-name table styling. Also the 18-page count: half its pages are photo pages with no information; KOM's BTS mosaic on page 8 already does that job once, which is the right number of times.

references.title: BASURERO electronic press kit (Eileen Cabiling, AFI Conservatory alumna, 2019; 16 pp, letter) — the typical peer, shown as the cautionary case
references.what_it_does_well: It is complete and honest: a table of contents on p01 with page references, a press contact, the poster, festival links, key cast and crew, director's statement, team bios, and (p09) the on-screen end quotes and the full crawl. Every fact a programmer needs is in it. Nothing is fabricated or padded. As information architecture it matches KOM's epk-spec almost item for item.
references.take_for_kom: The one thing it gets right that KOM currently gets wrong: bios and provenance are separated. Basurero's TEAM BIOS page (p06) prints Long bio, Mid bio (150 words) and Short bio (70 words) as labelled variants, and keeps its production notes elsewhere. KOM's page 7 prints its editorial provenance note inside the body copy. Adopt the labelled-variant idea only in the data (epk.json: bio_long / bio_short / notes), and print exactly one variant per person, the short one, so page 7 fits. Inference: the '7.1' field was written as a working document and pasted whole; the fix is in the data schema, not in para().
references.avoid: Everything visual. It is a Word export in Arial at 10 pt with a centred bold title, a ToC, hyperlinks pasted as raw URLs, and no images after the poster. This is what most film-school kits look like (of nine NFMLA-hosted short kits opened, six are this genre: Bartlett, Lunchbox, Basurero, Written By, Tomorrow, Spotless). KOM is already far past it; the only risk is regressing toward it when page 7 is rebuilt to 'make everything fit'. Do not shrink type below BODY-0.6 to fit; cut words.

principles: Peers publish very few PDF kits at all; the ones that exist are Word or Keynote exports. Inference from the corpus: a thesis kit that is one typeface, one hue and one image per page is already in the top few percent of its peer group. KOM's page 3 is the standard; the job is to bring pages 7, 9-11 to it, not to add anything.

One image, one job per page. Every peer kit that works (Blue Hour, Superhero) gives each page a single photograph at a fixed size and never lets a photograph and a paragraph compete for the same rectangle. KOM page 7 currently gives the still 1000 pt and the text 728 pt and both lose; either the still is the ghost (as on page 3) or the still is the page (as on page 9), never a full-bleed hero plus four paragraphs.

Roles and names sit on a shared axis. Right-aligned DIM role, left-aligned CREAM name from a common x, same size, tracked, 28 pt leading. Page 3 does it against the right margin at x=1222; page 7 and page 9 should do it against a centre or gutter axis with the same tracked() call, not a fixed +210 pt offset.

Bios are data with variants, not paragraphs with notes. Store long / short / provenance separately in epk.json, print one variant, fit() it to a fixed box, and never let a working note reach para(). Equal boxes per person (Blue Hour fails this; Superhero passes) is what makes a bio page read as fair.

A running identity per page. Blue Hour's tracked title top-right on every inside page and a page number bottom-right is the cheapest way the peers make eleven pages read as one object. KOM's pages 1-8 have the tracked 40 pt title with the 236 pt hairline; pages 9-11 have single-word bold titles at 48 pt margins. Inference: whichever way Luke rules on one-object-or-two, repeating one small tracked mark (title or page number) at one fixed position on all eleven pages resolves most of the seam without touching the settled Night Feeds form.

No caption blocks on images, no tech specs on the cover, no raw URLs. Every peer that does these looks like a student kit; KOM's link() primitive and the page 3 specs list already handle all three correctly.
references.not_found: No genuine AFI Conservatory thesis press-kit PDF (2022-2026) is publicly indexed; searches for AFI, USC, NYU Tisch, Chapman, UCLA, Columbia, CalArts, NFTS and La Fémis thesis 'press kit' PDFs returned only school pages, course catalogs and showcase listings. The Hicks Happy Hour (AFI thesis 2024, Tribeca 2025) official site hickshappyhour.com carries no press-kit link. The Climb EPK (CalArts faculty film, static1.squarespace.com) returned HTTP 404 with a browser user agent. The Eid Mubarak (USC MFA thesis, Oscar-longlisted) 'press kit' URL on newfilmmakersla.com resolved to a saved web page (Scribd/social icons), not the kit; nooreuceph.com exposes no PDF. Blue Hour is an AFI Directing Workshop for Women short, not a Conservatory thesis; Basurero is by an AFI alumna, not a thesis. Refs dirs eephus, janus-fournights and substance in the scratchpad were placed by another lane and were not examined here.

references.title: Janus Films — Godland press notes (2023, in-house designed, 5 pp, US Letter)
references.what_it_does_well: One type family (Freight) at exactly three sizes: 9 pt body, 12-13 pt section heads, 18 pt page heads; title 32 pt once. Page 2 is the model for a bio+credits page: portrait top-left (258 x 232 pt), DIRECTOR BIOGRAPHY under it, then a year-tabbed filmography (2022 / 2019 / 2017 ...), then a short DIRECTOR'S STATEMENT; the right column carries CAST then CREDITS as dot-leader pairs (role left in body weight, name right in the accent tone) on a 19-20 pt pitch, with a second still closing the column at the foot. Page 3-5 interview runs three 230 pt columns with italic questions and body answers, and every still is placed full-column-width and flush to the column edge, never floated inside text. Nothing is centered after the cover; margins are a constant 36 pt frame and the still on p1 sits inside that frame, not bled.
references.take_for_kom: Rebuild page 7 (cast) on the Godland p2 pattern, scaled x2.12 to the 1296 x 1728 sheet: still (Mace, 1.1.N) as a framed block at x=96 y=96 w=548 h=492 via cover(), the four bios as ONE left column x=96 width=548 in para() at 19 pt / 27 lead (Godland's 9/13 ratio), each opened by a label()-style role line ('MACE  |  ERIK ORJIAKO' in DIM small caps, tracked) and closed by a 'Prior credits' line set as a year-less filmography in DIM; the BILLED CAST list moves to a right column x=700 width=500 as role | name pairs on a 41 pt pitch (Godland's 19.5 pt x2.12), role in DIM and name in CREAM, using the same right-aligned convention page 3 already uses. The 'DRAFTS, NOT YET APPROVED' provenance paragraph is not copy and must be removed from the page entirely (keep it in epk.json under a key the builder never draws). Also take the count: Godland runs at three type sizes per page; KOM pages 1-8 should be audited to the same three (label 16-18, body 19-21, title 40) and anything else removed.
references.avoid: Do not import the rust accent colour or dot leaders; KOM's DIM/CREAM pair already does the role/name distinction and the dot leader is a hue-free flourish Clean Bank forbids. Do not copy Godland's centered cover with seven laurels; KOM's cover is the poster and the fact block is page 3.

references.title: Janus Films — Four Nights of a Dreamer press notes (2024 restoration release, in-house designed, 5 pp, US Letter)
references.what_it_does_well: The cover is the closest public analogue to KOM page 3's logic: one still, full-bleed across the top 53 percent of the sheet (0-420 of 792 pt), and everything else in the lower half arranged as two columns, contact on the left in a narrow 140 pt column and title + synopsis on the right in a 342 pt column; the title is the only large element (32 pt) and it is right-column-aligned, not centered. Page 2 sets a 251 pt text column (41 percent of the width) on the left and lets the still on the right run off the page edge (x 315 to 612), so the image and the text never compete for the same horizontal band; CAST and CREDITS occupy the lower right under the still, exactly the role-left / name-right pair on a 19 pt pitch. Page 5 is a two-column bio page whose right column is a year-tabbed filmography in a lighter tone, and the 8 pt fact strip ('France | 1971 | 82 minutes | Color | ...') is the only place pipes appear.
references.take_for_kom: Take the 'image owns one edge, text owns the other' rule and apply it to pages 5 and 7 the way page 3 already does. Page 5 (Filmmakers) currently alternates portraits left/right/left across three staggered rows, which is the one place the kit looks laid out rather than composed; set all three portraits in one column at x=96 w=310 (Four Nights' 140:342 split scaled gives 296:724, use 310/700 with a 96 gutter) and all three bios in one column at x=502 width=698, each portrait top-aligned to its own role line, so the page has one vertical seam like page 3 has. For page 7 the same seam: still cropped to run off the right edge (cover() with x=740 w=556 h=full-bleed to 1296) is an option the kit has not used yet and Four Nights p2 proves it works with a text column at 41 percent width. Measurement to take: Janus's body column is 41 percent of sheet width; KOM's page 5 bio column at 698/1296 is 54 percent and reads wider than it should, bring it to 530 pt (41 percent).
references.avoid: Do not take the boxed rust fact-strip or the centered publisher logo block; KOM has no logo and the fact block on page 3 already does this job in the right-aligned key/value form. Do not take the italic-question interview layout; KOM has no interview and inventing one is copy, not design.

references.title: Counter-reference: Janus/Sideshow 2025 press notes as distributed for Peter Hujar's Day, Resurrection and Caught by the Tides, plus The Substance (Mubi, Cannes 2024) and Eephus (Music Box, 2024)
references.what_it_does_well: These show what the trade actually ships in 2024-2025: Word-document press notes. The Janus 2025 notes (Hujar, Resurrection) are a centered laurel-and-still cover followed by a synopsis page that is one paragraph on white; Caught by the Tides is Century Gothic centered; The Substance (Cannes competition, Mubi) is Arial on Letter with no design at all. Eephus (Music Box) is the designed exception and it is 16:9 slides with a logo, pennant and signatures on every page. The useful lesson is negative: the press corps reads all of these without complaint, so a designed kit is a choice about the film's dignity, not a requirement, and the only designed ones that hold up (Godland, Four Nights) are the two that used one family, one accent, a fixed frame and left-aligned columns.
references.take_for_kom: One thing to take from the plain notes: every one of them puts a single-line fact strip (country | year | minutes | colour | language | aspect ratio) at the foot of page 1 and a PR contact block above it, and nothing else. KOM page 3 already has the facts as a key/value column; keep that, but note that the page-1 poster carries no contact at all and the plain-notes convention would put 'killerofmenmovie@gmail.com' as one 16 pt DIM line at y=1660 under the poster. Inference, not a ruling: the Night Feeds precedent likely does the same, check p01 there before adding it.
references.avoid: Everything else: centered headings, laurel rows across the top, the slide-deck format, per-page logos, signatures on stills, underlined link text in blue. KOM's link() already underlines in DIM; do not let it drift toward the Hujar blue.

principles: Image owns one edge, text owns the other. The two good Janus pages and KOM page 3 all share one vertical seam: still on one side (bled or framed), a single text column on the other, never a still floated inside running text. Pages 5 and 7 currently break this and are the two pages that look assembled; fix them by giving each a single seam (portraits x=96-406 / bios x=502-1200 on page 5; bios x=96-644 / billed cast x=700-1200 on page 7).

Three type sizes per page, then stop. Godland runs 9 / 12-13 / 18 pt with one 32 pt title on the cover; scaled x2.12 that is label 18, body 19-21 (27 lead), section head 26-28, page title 40. Audit pages 1-8 against that ladder and delete any size that is not on it; the small '@handle IMDB' line on page 5 at roughly 13 pt is the first casualty.

Column width is 41 percent of the sheet. Both Janus pages set the running text column at 251/612 pt; on 1296 that is 530 pt. KOM's bio columns at 698 pt are 54 percent and produce 95-character lines; bring para() width to 530-548 on pages 5 and 7 and let the freed width go to the image.

Role | name lists are a two-tone pair on a fixed pitch, not a paragraph. Godland and Four Nights: role in body weight, name in the accent tone, 19-20 pt pitch on a 9 pt body (2.1x). KOM's DIM/CREAM pair is the hue-free version; page 3 already does it right-aligned at 41 pt pitch (inference from the render). Page 7's BILLED CAST must be drawn with the same tracked() calls as page 3, never with para().

Provenance is not copy. Nothing in any of the eight kits prints its own editorial notes. The 'DRAFTS, NOT YET APPROVED' text on page 7 comes from a field the builder should never draw; move it to a sidecar key in epk.json (e.g. bios_provenance) and have build-epk-kit.py read only the approved bio string.

The plain notes prove restraint costs nothing. Distributors with the strongest brands (A24, Neon, Mubi) ship undesigned Word notes; the press reads them. Every element KOM adds beyond the Godland set (still, title, body, role|name list, fact strip, contact) is a personality claim and should be argued for individually, which is the Clean Bank rule restated from the trade's side.
references.not_found: A24, Neon, Focus Features, Searchlight and Kino Lorber: no public press-notes PDFs could be located. Searchlight's press site (press.searchlightpictures.com) is gated behind EPK.TV registration and I did not register; A24's a24films.com/notes is an editorial page, not press notes; Neon's neonrated.com film pages carry no PDF links; Kino Lorber film pages (teachers-lounge, fallen-leaves, dahomey, green-border) returned no .pdf hrefs to a plain curl. Mubi: the only public kit found was The Substance via a festival mirror (files.eventival.com), which is an undesigned Word export and is filed as a counter-reference. Cannes CDN searches for the 2025 Neon/Mubi titles (Sentimental Value, Sirat, The Secret Agent, It Was Just an Accident) returned festival documents, not film kits. The two designed references are therefore both Janus Films; that is a real gap in the lane, not a choice.

references.title: John Szarkowski, Looking at Photographs (MoMA, 1973) — verso column / recto plate spreads
references.what_it_does_well: This is the purest public instance of the lane: 100 spreads, every one a single column of text on the verso facing a single plate on the recto, and it never varies. Measured off the p05 spread (page 621 x 782 pt in the scan; scan is 13 spreads, no live text): the text column runs x = 0.29 to 0.91 of the page width, i.e. it is pushed toward the gutter with a small inner margin (~56 pt) and a very large outer margin (~181 pt), so the column leans into the picture across the gutter and the empty paper sits on the outside. The header block starts low, at 0.25 of page height, and the last line lands at ~0.73; the folio sits alone at 0.92. Measure is ~384 pt and the first line of the Shew entry is 74 characters, so the book runs at 72-76 characters per line, justified. The plate on the recto has inner margin ~100 pt, outer ~74 pt, top ~0.22 H, bottom ~0.78 H: it is a framed object with its own paper margin, never full bleed, and each plate is scaled to its own proportions rather than to a fixed box. The header hierarchy uses ONE type size: artist name in letterspaced capitals, dates in roman beneath, a hairline the width of the column, then title / medium / credit in roman. No bold, no second size, no colour; rank is carried by caps, italic, a rule, and space. About 55 percent of every page is empty paper. The whole spread is a picture and a caption, at book scale.
references.take_for_kom: Rebuild page 7 (cast) as a Szarkowski verso: keep the still as a framed plate on the left rather than a full-bleed banner, and give each actor the exact header block: ROLE in DIM tracked caps, NAME in CREAM on the next line, a hairline the width of the text column (the same 236 pt hairline primitive that sits under the p03 title, but stretched to the column measure), then the bio as a para(). Concretely on the 1296 x 1728 page: plate via cover(c, im, x=74, y=192, w=480, h=~640, alpha=1.0) at full opacity (Szarkowski's plate has its own margin: 74 pt matches the 74 pt right margin p03 already uses at x=1222); text column from x=640 to x=1222 (measure 582 pt), flush-left, ragged-right, Baskerville Regular 17-18 pt on 24 pt lead, which at Baskerville's ~0.45 em average width gives ~70 cpl, inside Bringhurst's 45-75 band. Start the first header block at y = 0.25 H = 432 pt, as Szarkowski does, and put nothing above it but the tracked title. Cap each bio at 90 words (see Smithsonian below) so four billed actors fit with the hairline blocks between them; BILLED CAST becomes a second, DIM, right-aligned key list at x=1222 below the bios or on the p03 column pattern. Never print the provenance notes: the builder must read only the approved bio text from epk.json (7.1's notes are field metadata, not copy) — this is the actual bug that produced the current page.
references.avoid: Do not copy its justified setting: Szarkowski justifies at 74 cpl in a metal-type book with hand hyphenation; in ReportLab at 582 pt justified Baskerville will river. Ragged-right at ~66-70 cpl is the safe equivalent. Also do not copy its centered header block onto a page whose other elements are right-aligned to x=1222; on KOM the header should share the bio column's left edge (Szarkowski's centered head is a book convention, not a rule).

references.title: Walker Evans, American Photographs (MoMA, 1938; 75th-anniversary preview PDF) — blank verso, plate recto
references.what_it_does_well: The 1938 Evans/Kirstein design is the extreme of the lane: the verso carries nothing but a folio (measured in the PDF: 36 pt from the left edge, at 0.89 of page height) and the recto carries one plate with a real paper margin on every side. Measured across ten plates in the PDF (spread 563 x 646 pt): top margins vary from 16 to 108 pt and plate widths from ~300 to ~520 pt, so each picture is placed by hand at its own size, yet the right-hand paper margin stays within a narrow band, which is why the sequence reads as one object. The essay pages (p15-16) are two ~62-character columns of small roman with an italic quotation set in the same size, no bold anywhere, and a page-number in the outer bottom corner. The book's authority comes from what is withheld: no captions on the plate page (titles are listed at the back), no rules, no ornaments, 70 percent of the paper empty.
references.take_for_kom: Take the Evans restraint for the stills-only pages and for p07's plate: no captions under stills (already the rule), and a plate that keeps a constant right-hand or left-hand edge while its size and top vary with the frame. For the credit pages 9-11 the Evans essay pages are the counter-argument to the Night Feeds Bold: an eleven-page object holds together when one weight and one size carry everything and rank comes from caps, italic and tone. Inference, not measurement: the Bold on 9-11 is the single thing making the kit read as two objects; the Evans and Szarkowski pages show a kit can go from plate to prose to list without changing weight. If Luke rules one object, drop Bold and reuse p03's DIM/CREAM key-value pattern for credits, with tracked(c, ...) caps for department heads at the same size as the names.
references.avoid: Do not imitate the blank verso literally on a PDF read on screen: a wholly empty page in a festival kit reads as an error, not as rest. The transferable idea is the margin around the plate, not the empty facing page.

references.title: Jan Tschichold, Penguin Composition Rules (1947) and the Van de Graaf / Tschichold page canon; Bringhurst measure rules; Smithsonian label rules
references.what_it_does_well: These are the measurable rules behind the two books above. Tschichold's Penguin rules (the infolio.es PDF is a Spanish translation of the 1947 booklet; English text confirmed via Wikipedia 'Penguin Composition Rules'): word-spacing no wider than the thickness of an 'i' at the text size; capitals always letterspaced; no bold in book text; paragraph indent one em, none after a heading; one type size for text with rank carried by caps, small caps and italic. Tschichold's canon (Wikipedia 'Canons of page construction'): margins inner:top:outer:bottom = 1 : R : 2 : 2R for a page of proportion 1:R, with the type-area height equal to the page width; bottom margin largest 'because we hold the book by the lower margin'. Bringhurst (via Wikipedia 'Line length'): 45-75 characters per line, 66 ideal, measure roughly 30 times the type size, 20-40 acceptable; widen leading as the measure widens. Smithsonian Guidelines for Accessible Exhibition Design, section III (page 21 of the PDF): max 55 characters per line, 45-50 preferable; label length 75-100 words maximum; sentences no more than 25 words, 15 preferable; 1.5 line spacing.
references.take_for_kom: Two direct numbers. (1) The KOM page is 1296 x 1728 pt, exactly 3:4, so R = 4/3 and the Tschichold canon with unit = page width / 9 = 144 pt gives inner 144, top 192, outer 288, bottom 384 pt and a type area of 864 x 1296 pt. Treating the image side as 'inner' this puts a text column's outer edge at 1296 - 288 = 1008 and its foot at 1728 - 384 = 1344. p03 sits at x=1222 with the footer links ending near y=1620; the canon says the largest empty space belongs at the foot, and p03's contact block at 0.94 H fights that. A gentler application: keep x=1222, but reserve a 192 pt foot (nothing below y=1536) on every text page and let the columns start no higher than y=192. (2) Measure: the director's statement on p04 runs ~75-80 cpl at ~19 pt (measured from the render: the column is ~720 pt wide) and is set ragged-LEFT (right-aligned prose), which makes the eye hunt for each line start over 30 lines; Bringhurst and Tschichold both put this beyond the band. Set para() for p04 with align='left', x = 1222 - 600, width=600 for ~66 cpl at 18-19 pt, right edge still on the p03 spine at 1222. This touches a settled decision in sexy-pass-changes (the right-aligned statement) and must be flagged. Smithsonian's 75-100 word cap is the edit rule for cast bios and the director bio: the current p07 bios are 110-140 words each, which is why they cannot share a page with the plate.
references.avoid: Do not apply the Smithsonian 55 cpl or its sans-serif advice to the kit: those are wall-reading numbers at one metre; a PDF read at arm's length takes Bringhurst's 66. And do not chase the golden canon's exact 864 x 1296 block; it was derived for a bound codex with a gutter and on a single-page PDF it is a sanity check on margins, not a grid to draw.

principles: The image is an object with its own margin, not a background. Szarkowski's plate keeps 74-100 pt of paper on every side; Evans varies size and top but holds one edge. On KOM the ghosted still on p03 works because the Elder occupies the left third and fades before the column; on p07 the full-bleed banner over 60 percent of the page inverts the ratio and leaves the text no room. Frame the plate (cover() with x=74, full alpha) or ghost it (ground() at alpha 0.22), never bleed it on a text page.

One weight, one size, rank by caps / tone / rule / space. Szarkowski's header block and Evans's essay pages use no bold and no second size; hierarchy is letterspaced caps, roman, a hairline, and white space. KOM pages 1-8 already do this with DIM keys and CREAM values; the Bold on 9-11 is the one element with no precedent in the lane and is the likeliest reason the kit reads as two objects (inference).

Measure 60-70 characters per line, flush-left for prose. Bringhurst's 45-75 with 66 ideal; Szarkowski runs 72-76 justified in metal. At Baskerville Regular 17-19 pt that is a 560-620 pt column on the 1296 pt page. Right-aligned ragged-left is fine for key-value lists (p03) and fails for 30-line paragraphs (p04): keep the spine at x=1222 but let prose columns be flush-left with their right edge on the spine.

Start low, end early, leave the foot empty. Szarkowski's first line sits at 0.25 H and his last at 0.73 H; Tschichold's canon makes the bottom margin the largest (384 pt on a 3:4 page of this size). A page that fills to 0.94 H, as p03's links and p07 do, reads as crowded even when the type is small. Reserve at least 192 pt of ground at the foot of every text page.

Edit to the page, not the page to the copy. Smithsonian caps a label at 75-100 words; Szarkowski's entries are 250-300 words for a whole page. Four cast bios plus a plate on one 1296 x 1728 page only work at ~90 words each. Cutting copy is the design move that makes 'figure left, column right' possible; shrinking type is the template move that breaks it.

What makes it art rather than a template is consistency of the invariant and freedom in the variable: Evans holds the paper margin and lets every plate change size; Szarkowski holds the column and lets every picture change proportion; p03 holds the right spine at 1222 and lets the Elder sit where the frame put her. Pick one invariant per page family (the spine at 1222 for pages 1-8) and let the still be the only thing that moves.

references.what_it_does_well: Twenty A4 pages, one page per nominee, the same skeleton fifteen times: a 16:9 still across the top third, a black title bar with TITLE at left and COUNTRY / MINS / YEAR at right, then Director, Producers, Synopsis, Director's Biography, a pull quote, and an Awards list in small type. references.title: ALI (Adnan Al Rajeev, KATALOG) — press kit, Festival de Cannes 2025 Short Films Competition, Special Mention of the Short Film Jury
references.what_it_does_well: Six white A4 pages exported from a word processor: cover with the Cannes mark, LOGLINE / SYNOPSIS, BIOGRAPHY, TECHNICAL DETAILS, DIRECTOR'S STATEMENT, PRODUCTION COMPANY. No stills inside. It is the floor of the lane, and it went to Cannes and won a mention: the jury never saw the kit. Its one virtue is the TECHNICAL DETAILS page, a fixed field list (TITLE, COUNTRIES, YEAR OF PRODUCTION, LANGUAGE, GENRE, DURATION, FORMAT, ASPECT RATIO, then the department heads and the sales agent) that a festival's print traffic can lift line by line.
references.take_for_kom: A deflationary counterweight to the whole exercise: the kit's job is to be findable and liftable, and KOM's page 3 already does the ALI technical page better (same field list, right-aligned at x=1222, live links). The one thing to take is the field ALI has and KOM's page 3 lacks: a 'SALES / DISTRIBUTION' or 'FESTIVAL CONTACT' line separate from the rights holder, because a programmer contacts the producer, not AFI's rights office. Add it to the RIGHTS block in page_programmer() as a fourth key/value row from epk.json (Ruoxiao Li's email if she is the festival contact), one line, no new page.
references.avoid: Everything else: the word-processor typesetting, letterspaced headings in a bold sans, all-caps body facts, no stills, white ground. Do not let the crew-audit temptation ('Sound: Bien Sparks') turn KOM page 3 into a full crew list; that is page 10's job.

principles: Half-frame rule. The best pages in this lane give the still one vertical half and the text the other and never mix them (Vultures p4/p7/p10; KOM page 3). Ghosting is the only sanctioned exception, and only at the ratified 0.16-0.22 alpha under a 0.50-0.55 scrim. Page 7's hero-band-plus-text-block is the one page in KOM that breaks the rule, and it is the broken page.

A list is a list. Cast and crew are set as role/name pairs, role DIM and name CREAM, one pair per line or role stacked over name, never as sentences. Bios have their own form (portrait + ROLE | NAME lockup + paragraph, pages 5-6) and their own page. Provenance notes, drafts and fact-check remarks in a JSON field are data, not copy; the builder gates them (7.1 beginning 'DRAFTS' renders as empty).

Three numbers before any prose: country, minutes, year. Every kit in the lane puts them beside the title of the first content page (ShortsTV strap, Vultures p10, ALI p4). KOM page 2 should carry them as one DIM tracked line drawn from page-3 fields, so a programmer never has to turn the page to learn it is a 13-minute film.

One register for the whole object. Vultures is eleven pages, one face, one weight family for headings and one for body, one hue, front to back; the credits page is simply the same register with more names on it. Inference from the lane: a kit whose credit pages change face weight, margin and ground recipe reads as two objects stapled together, and no reference in the lane does that. If the open ruling goes 'one object', pages 9-11 inherit the page-3 recipe (Regular/SemiBold, 74 pt margins, ghost at 0.22/0.50 or a dark half-frame); if it goes 'two objects', the break should be declared by a divider page, not discovered on page 9.

Awards and selections are text, not badges. The Cannes kits carry one selection mark on the cover and nothing else; the Oscar omnibus lists awards as small lines under a label. When KOM's laurels arrive they go into the page-3 column as lines above RIGHTS, in DIM, never as laurel art.

Measure the reference before copying it. Vultures sets its cast/crew at 32-36 pt on a 2430 pt page (1.3-1.5% of width); KOM's BODY / 17 pt on 1296 pt is 1.3%, so the existing sizes are already right and the fix on page 7 is composition (which half, how many lines, where the gate is), not type. The lane's floor (ALI) won a Cannes mention on six word-processor pages: the picture and the facts do the work, so every change that is not the picture or the facts is suspect.

critics.what_works:
Looked at p05, p06, p03 (north star), Night Feeds p05/p06, all four BTS candidates, the four headshot masters, and the geometry from the code itself (/usr/bin/python3 with reportlab 5.0.0 imports the kit cleanly; measured: page 5 blocks 250/436/436 pt with 79 pt gaps, last block 183 pt above the foot; page 6 blocks 436/436 with 216 pt gaps above, between and below).

The block anatomy is right and is already the kit's best prose idiom: ROLE | NAME in Bask-SB 21 tracked 2.2, the 333 x 396 portrait, the 19/30 bio on a 767 pt measure, the 48 pt gutter. The DP block on page 5 (portrait at x=74, text at x=455) is the closest thing in the kit to the page 3 composition Luke named: image left third, words right. Ruoxiao Li's and You Wu's blocks mirror it cleanly. The four headshots are the film's own light (hard side key, sepia-black) and they dissolve into GROUND with no visible rectangle: that is why these two pages, uniquely in the kit, must NOT carry a ghost still. A ghost at page 3's mean L ~17 would reveal every portrait's edge as a box. The empty ground here is doing a job. The FILMMAKERS title on page 5 under the title law, and page 6 running headless as a continuation, both read as one document, unlike Night Feeds p05/p06, which the KOM pages already beat on every count (NF sets 150+ words of all-caps 9 pt with the name run into the first sentence; a laptop reader cannot read it without zooming). Bios here are 45 to 111 words, sentence case, 19 pt: on a laptop at ~54 % (page at 700 px wide) that is ~10 px x-height text, readable.

What is merely ordinary: page 5 opens on a hole (the director's block is words at the left with 767 pt of nothing beside it where every other block has a face); page 6's two blocks float at thirds with three equal 216 pt voids, which reads as a slide, not a page; the handles and IMDB are the smallest text on the spread (14.2 pt, ~7.7 px on a laptop) with no cue that they are links, while page 3 already established the kit's link idiom (0.5 pt DIM underline). Across the page turn the alternation restarts (L R L | L R), so a reader scrolling on a laptop sees two left portraits in a row at the seam.

findings.what: The director has no face on page 5. A programmer opens the filmmaker pages on the one person they most want to see and finds a hole.

findings.change: Use KOM_Day3_TheFarm-43 (the director alone, in profile at the monitor, hand at chin, headphones), NOT -45 or -46: in any 0.84 crop that keeps his face at 40 % height, -45 and -46 carry a second man's face at the left edge (a two-shot beside four single headshots; the second man is unidentified) and -93 is a wide three-shot whose centre figure's head would be ~12 % of the box with two crew backs in frame. critics.what_works: Still 5 is the right hero and must stay: of the 41 frames it is the only one with Mace upright, facing near-camera, lit by the film's signature light (the barn slats), and at un-letterboxed mean L 72.9 it is the brightest frame that is still the film's own grade (still 4 at L 102 is cooler and shows him bent over; 34/35/40 are night frames at L 21-36 that would print as mud at 1.0). After the poster's flat colour, this is the frame that says 'photographed film'. The two-band structure (full-bleed hero above, text on bare GROUND below, no title, no caption) is correct for this page: the poster is the title, and a ghost under the text band would put two image treatments on one page. The type is right: the 26/40 to 22/34.5 step, DIM 15.6 tracked labels, mixed-case running text, the text block hard-edged at x = M = 74 (which mirrors page 3's hard edge at W - M = 1222: verso/recto logic across the spread, a real relationship, keep it). The PROOF slug at 9.5 DIM on the 33 pt line is doing its job and stays until 2.1/2.2 are filled. Measured: the current block runs from the LOGLINE baseline 950 pt from the top to the last synopsis baseline 1490 pt from the top (540 pt), leaving 238 pt to the foot (164 above the margin); the 90 : 164 split of the remainder is roughly 3 : 5, which is why the page does not feel broken even though nothing chose that ratio.

findings.what: The hero crop amputates the frame's meaning. cover() fits the 2.38:1 still (1920 x 806 px after unletterbox) into 1296 x 860 pt, a 1.51:1 box, so sc = 860/806 and the crop keeps 1215 of 1920 px: 63% of the width, x 352-1567. Everything left of x 352 is gone, and that is where the frame's second figure stands: a white man in a waistcoat at the left edge, watching Mace (inference from costume and the synopsis: this is Master Kenner, the owner who stages the bouts; Luke can confirm). The raised hand with the weight also kisses the top edge. What survives is a bare-chested man with a raised fist against timber, centred on the page: a physique shot, not the story. The full frame is the synopsis in one image: the owner at the edge, the fighter in the light, the wager between them.
findings.why: This is the first photograph a programmer sees after the poster, and it is the cinematographer's own composition; a press kit that crops 37% out of the DP's frame is re-composing his shot. At laptop fit-to-height the 3:2 crop reads as a generic 'strong man' still; the 2.38-ish band with the owner in it reads as a film with a premise. critics.what_works: The credit-card rhythm itself is sound and should be left alone: the right-aligned role / left-aligned name pairs on one gutter, the 28 pt slot grid on CREW, departments parted by one blank slot with no headings (the reference's quietest device, and the kit's Clean Bank rule kept), the lead cast pair set one size up and everything else flat, extras and thanks in mirrored three-column blocks, the fellows by discipline, and the legal block anchored a fixed 90 pt above the AFI box. The data discipline is exemplary: nothing retyped, gaps printed as the data reads, every name parsed from epk.json at build time, and the legibility gate that refuses a variant it cannot read. Page 9's composition (column in the black left third, image in the right) is the correct translation of Night Feeds p09 and its CAST group under the key credits is well spaced (84 pt lead-in, 64 pt after the label, the lead row at 36 pt). Page 11's order (extras, thanks, slots, Avid, boilerplate, fellows, copyright, AFI) is the reference's order and reads as a real end card. The one structural fact a builder must know before touching any still on these pages: a 2.39:1 frame covered to a 1296 x 1728 page keeps only 604 of 1920 source pixels (31 percent of the width). The Night Feeds form works on that kit's near-square frames; on this film's frames the still is texture by construction, and the choice of still must be made on the crop, not the frame.

Provenance is data, never copy. Anything in a JSON field that is not a bio, a name or a fact is gated by the builder and surfaces, if at all, as the one proof-slug class (9.5 pt DIM at the 33 pt mark line).
